title: Streetwear
subtitle: A Full-Stack Leather, Denim & Boots Store
alt: Streetwear online store home page with leather jackets, denim and boots
summary: A full-stack fashion store with a 200-product catalog, a no-code admin and a 360° 3D outfit viewer, running on Cloudflare's global network.
overview: Streetwear is a complete online store for leather jackets, denim and boots that I designed and engineered end to end: an editorial storefront, a REST API, a database, and an admin panel the owner can run without touching code. A Three.js mannequin lets shoppers rotate an outfit in 360° and see it recoloured per look. It is a demo store, so there is no online payment yet.
challenge: The goal was a store that feels like a real fashion brand, not a template: light editorial design, smooth motion, a 200-product catalog that stays fast, and every piece of content (products, categories, menus, pages, home sections, outfits) editable by a non-developer. It also had to run on the free tier of a global edge platform, where a Worker cannot simply call another site's URL.
role: Designed the visual system (tokens, typography, scroll and text-reveal animation) and built every storefront page: home, shop, categories, product, checkout, outfits, search, wishlist and customer accounts.
Built the Express API on Workers with service bindings between the storefront and the API, so both deploy as one product from a single command.
Made checkout safe: prices are recalculated on the server and stock is checked in one atomic database batch, so an order cannot oversell an item.
Built the admin panel (login, dashboard, orders, products, categories, menus, pages, outfits, reviews, customers, media, settings) and the Three.js 360° outfit viewer.
impact: 200-product catalog live and manageable from the admin, with reviews stored in MongoDB and orders in D1.
Oversell-proof checkout and server-side pricing, so the browser can never set its own price.
Served from Cloudflare's edge network, which suits visitors in Bangladesh and abroad alike.
One-command deployment (`npm run deploy`) for both API and storefront, with a documented rollback path.

title: Parfume Store
subtitle: Fragrance e-commerce
alt: Parfume Store fragrance e-commerce website built on WooCommerce
summary: A fragrance e-commerce store on WooCommerce and Elementor, with a slide-out cart drawer that keeps shoppers browsing.
overview: Parfume Store is a live fragrance shop built on WordPress, WooCommerce and Elementor. I designed the product layouts and built a slide-out cart drawer so shoppers can add several perfumes without ever leaving the page they are on.
challenge: Fragrance buyers compare many bottles before they decide. A cart that sends them to a separate page on every add interrupts that habit and costs sales. The store also needed to stay editable by the owner in Elementor rather than locked behind custom code.
role: Built the storefront in Elementor with consistent product cards, clear pricing and a mobile-first layout.
Implemented a slide-out cart drawer on top of WooCommerce so adding to cart no longer interrupts browsing.
Set up the catalog structure and checkout flow so the owner can add products and edit pages on their own.
impact: Shoppers can keep browsing while their cart updates in place, which suits the compare-before-you-buy way people shop for perfume.
The owner manages products and pages in Elementor and WooCommerce without a developer.
Live on its own domain at parfumerep.com.

title: FootSeason
subtitle: Football jersey store
alt: FootSeason football jersey online store with team collections
summary: A football jersey store on WooCommerce and Elementor, with organized team collections and a smooth path from browsing to checkout.
overview: FootSeason sells football jerseys online. I built it on WordPress, WooCommerce and Elementor with a clean product layout, jerseys grouped into team collections, and a short path from browsing to checkout.
challenge: A jersey shop has a lot of near-identical products across many teams and sizes. Without clear structure, shoppers get lost, and the owner cannot keep the catalog tidy as it grows.
role: Planned the catalog around team collections and categories so every jersey has an obvious home.
Designed and built the product, collection and checkout pages in Elementor, tuned for phones first.
Configured WooCommerce product options and checkout so buying a jersey takes only a few steps.
impact: Fans can find their team's jerseys in a click or two through organized collections.
A tidy catalog structure the owner can keep extending without redesigning.
Live and taking visitors at footseason.com.

title: Extraction
subtitle: 2D top-down shooter game
alt: Extraction top-down shooter game screenshot with loot crates and enemies
summary: A top-down extraction shooter you play in the browser or on Android, with solo raids and online multiplayer for up to 15 players.
overview: Extraction is a top-down shooter where you deploy into a random map full of enemies and loot, then reach the green zone and survive to escape. Get out alive and you keep your loot; die and you lose everything you brought. It started as a solo game and now includes online player-versus-player matches and an Android app.
challenge: A real-time multiplayer game has to feel responsive on a phone's mobile connection, while staying cheap to run. I also wanted every piece of art and sound generated in code, so the game stays small and loads fast.
role: Designed and programmed the whole game: combat, enemy AI, loot, hideout, bombs and the raid loop, written as plain, tested logic separate from the drawing layer.
Built online multiplayer rooms (free-for-all or teams, up to 15 players) with one Cloudflare Durable Object per room and client-side prediction and interpolation.
Packaged the game as a signed Android app with Capacitor, and shipped it from the same deploy as the web version.
impact: An automated suite of more than 240 tests covers the game rules, so new features don't quietly break old ones.
The Android app is roughly 1.3 MB because art and sound are generated in code.
No database to run: solo progress saves in the browser and multiplayer rooms hold no stored data.

title: 3D 360° Viewer
subtitle: 3D portfolio, under development
alt: 3D portfolio website with a 360 degree viewer and curved photo gallery
summary: A 3D portfolio with a 360° model viewer and a curved 3D photo gallery, plus an admin panel for every upload.
overview: This is an experiment in making a portfolio feel like a place rather than a page: a 360° 3D model of the owner in the hero, a curved 3D photo gallery beneath it, About and Contact pages, and an admin panel for all uploads. It is still under development.
challenge: 3D on the web is easy to make slow. Photos had to look sharp in a 3D ribbon without shipping megabytes, a model file had to stay small enough to load quickly, and the owner needed to manage it all without code.
role: Built the Three.js 360° viewer and the curved ribbon gallery, with a click-through photo panel.
Wrote an admin that resizes every upload in the browser and converts it to WebP before it is stored.
Added sign-in, model upload limits and a local-storage fallback so the site can be developed without a database.
impact: Each photo is converted automatically to a full view of about 150–350 KB and a gallery thumbnail of about 40–90 KB, so the 3D gallery stays light.
The owner uploads photos and a .glb model from the admin, and they appear on the homepage straight away.
Deployed on Cloudflare Workers; work is still in progress.

title: Vira Skin Care
subtitle: Skin care brand
alt: Vira Skin Care Shopify storefront for a premium skin care brand
summary: A Shopify storefront for a premium skin care brand, with a clean layout and streamlined checkout.
overview: Vira Skin Care is a Shopify store concept for a premium skin care brand. I customised the theme so the products, ingredients and brand story take centre stage, and kept the path to checkout short.
challenge: Skin care shoppers buy on trust and on how clean a brand feels. A cluttered theme or a long checkout works against that, so the design had to be calm, quick, and clear about what each product does.
role: Adapted the Shopify theme with Liquid and CSS to a restrained, premium look that matches the brand.
Structured collections and product pages so benefits, details and the add-to-cart button are all visible without hunting.
Kept the checkout path short and tested the store across phone, tablet and desktop.
impact: A calm, uncluttered storefront that reads as premium on the first screen.
Short route from product to checkout, which is the part of a Shopify store that matters most for sales.
This is a preview store (password: limon) shared as a sample of Shopify work.

title: Baaizgar
subtitle: Clothing store, front end only
alt: Baaizgar clothing store front end for men, women and kids
summary: A hand-coded clothing storefront for men, women and kids, built with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
overview: Baaizgar is a front-end-only clothing store: classic, comfortable clothing for men, women and kids, from relaxed denim to easy everyday layers. It is written by hand in HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no framework, and hosted for free on GitHub Pages.
challenge: The point was to prove that a good-looking, responsive shop front doesn't need a heavy framework. Everything had to load quickly on a normal phone connection and stay easy to change.
role: Designed the layout and product browsing for men, women and kids sections.
Wrote all HTML, CSS and JavaScript by hand, with a responsive grid and no dependencies.
Published it on GitHub Pages so it costs nothing to host.
impact: A fast, dependency-free front end with no framework weight to download.
Free hosting and instant deploys through GitHub.
Front end only for now; it is a base that can be connected to a real back end and payments later.

title: Money Tracker
subtitle: Student budgeting app for Android
alt: Money Tracker budgeting app screens showing weekly budget and charts
summary: A student-friendly budgeting app with a weekly budget, monthly charts, savings goals and shareable summaries, built with React Native and Cloudflare.
overview: Money Tracker is a minimalist money app for students: a weekly budget, income tracking, monthly stats, savings goals, a choice of currency, a daily reminder, bill splitting and backup. Optional Google sign-in syncs data between phones and creates shareable monthly summaries. The link on this page downloads the Android APK.
challenge: Students want something quicker than a spreadsheet and simpler than a banking app. It had to work fully offline, and when sync is switched on, merge changes from two phones without losing anyone's data.
role: Designed and built the app screens (Home, Stats, Goals, More) and the charts and share card.
Wrote the sync rules that merge data between devices, and the Worker API with a D1 database for sign-in checks, sync, share links and account deletion.
Set up builds and over-the-air updates so fixes reach installed phones without a reinstall.
impact: Works fully offline; cloud sync is optional and opt-in.
Screen and logic changes reach installed phones through over-the-air updates.
Shareable monthly summaries and an account-deletion route, so users stay in control of their data.

title: Home Cleaning Service
subtitle: Service business website
alt: Home cleaning service website with service list and contact call to action
summary: A WordPress site for a home cleaning business that presents its services clearly and makes it easy to get in touch.
overview: A WordPress website for a home cleaning service in Bangladesh. It lists the services in plain language and puts a way to contact the business within reach on every page.
challenge: Local service customers decide fast. The site had to explain what is offered, build trust and give them an obvious next step, all on a phone, without relying on a heavy page builder setup.
role: Planned the page structure around services, trust and contact.
Built the site in WordPress with clear service sections and prominent call-to-action buttons.
Tested the layout across phone, tablet and desktop.
impact: Visitors see what the business offers and how to reach it within a screen or two.
Easy for the owner to update service text and photos.
Currently a development preview, shared as a sample of local service-business work.
